transcript:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2025-08-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jin Park (Redwood SE), María Lopez (OpalNorth Head of Search), Tom Nguyen (OpalNorth Eng Mgr), Aisha Khan (OpalNorth Data Scientist)
Recording ID: fire-20250811-opalnorth-01

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto):
- Quick hosted API demo showing embeddings and reranker endpoints.
- Discussed relevance tradeoffs (latency vs cost), VPC/private options, SOC2 and data residency.
- Agreed next steps to run a benchmark on a 1M doc sample and send pilot pricing.

TOPICS COVERED:
- OpalNorth current stack and pain points
- Redwood hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints (API walkthrough)
- Console: model selection + Optimize recommendations
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, retention
- Pilot scope + benchmarks

ACTION ITEMS (captured):
- Samir to send pricing + SOW by Thu 8/14
- Jin to prepare benchmark script and infra checklist
- Aisha to share anonymized dataset

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:08] María: Hi, María here, Head of Search at OpalNorth. We're reworking our product search relevance right now.
[00:13] Tom: Tom, engineering manager, I'll own the pilot infra.
[00:16] Aisha: Aisha, data scientist, I'll be running the evaluation and tuning.
[00:19] Jin: Jin Park, solutions engineer, I'll walk through the API and demo the reranker.
[00:24] Samir: Great. We have about 45 minutes of content and then we can take Q&A. The goal: show hosted embeddings + rerank flow and give you a clear pilot path.

[00:40] María: Quick context — currently we use a hybrid vector + BM25 stack. We index ~1.2M product specs, latency requirements are tight for PLG funnels. We saw cost balloon with our current embed provider, and re-rank quality is sometimes brittle.
[01:02] Tom: Also need to ensure we can do everything within our EU region for residency.
[01:07] Samir: Absolutely. We'll show the hosted flow and how we pin region + model. Also, we support dedicated and private deployments if you need VPC.

[01:20] Jin: Okay I'll share my screen — jumping into the Redwood Console. (brief pause) screen share glitch, sorry — there we go.
[01:31] Jin: Starting with the embeddings endpoint: you can see model catalog on the left. For this demo I'm using a mid-sized open model we've tuned — label says "rwd-embed-small-v2" — it's optimized for semantic recall / compact vectors. The API payload is straightforward, POST vectors/generate-embeddings with batching.
[01:52] (Aisha: mmm-hmm)
[01:55] Jin: Note: there is a cache key recommendation — Redwood Optimize suggests prefix caching for product titles to reduce token cost when users repeat similar queries. The console shows recommended batch size 128 for our observed sequence length.
[02:11] María: That auto-suggested batch size — is that per request or internal?
[02:15] Jin: It's an internal suggestion for optimal throughput; you can override in the client. The runtime will do smart batching and KV cache reuse. (note: transcript reads "K V cash" later).

[02:30] Jin: Now the reranker endpoint — this is the two-step flow we usually recommend: 1) retrieve top-K using your vector index (we show a Redis/FAISS example), 2) call Redwood rerank endpoint with the bubble of candidates and the original query. The reranker uses both embeddings and a cross-attention model to score relevance.
[02:56] Tom: What's the average latency we'd expect for the rerank call at K=20?
[03:01] Jin: For hosted small-mid models, typical p95 is ~120-180ms for rerank(20) in our EU region. For stricter SLOs, we can route to a dedicated pool or the lower-latency variant. There's a latency vs cost tradeoff — reranking across a large K increases compute.
[03:19] María: So if we do a two-phase approach — dense retrieve top 200 then rerank top 20 — costs will add up. Any tooling to estimate that?
[03:28] Jin: Yes, Redwood Console has a cost estimator tied to token profiles and calls. Optimize also gives batch + quantization recommendations; for example quantizing the reranker to int8 reduces cost ~2.4x with small quality delta. We'll show the Optimize tab in a sec.

[03:45] Samir: Quick question: what's your latency SLO for search?
[03:48] María: Under 200ms p95 ideally for product listing context — search is a high conversion path.
[03:54] Tom: For API hops we can accept 2-3 calls if each is fast.

[04:05] Jin: Switching to the Optimize tab — here you can upload workload traces or we can ingest logs. Optimize runs simulations and gives recommendations: model variant, batch sizes, and cache keys. For your product pages it suggests caching the first 64 tokens of common queries.
[04:26] Aisha: How accurate are the quality estimates? We need to avoid regressions for SKU disambiguation.
[04:31] Jin: We do evaluation against your held-out queries if you provide a labelled set. Optimize shows expected MAP/recall deltas for each recommendation. It's a prediction, not a guarantee, but it's been reliable in our pilots.

[04:50] (screen transition)
[04:55] Jin: Now I'll run a live sample. I'll call embeddings endpoint with 3 product title examples... sending request... response in 70ms. The vectors are 768-d floats by default, we also support 256-d and quantized variants.
[05:15] Tom: That 70ms includes network, right?
[05:17] Jin: Yes, that's from us in EU region — demo infra is colocated.

[05:25] Jin: Next, a mock retrieval + rerank. I have a candidate list of 25 items. Calling the rerank endpoint... (typing) — rerank returns scored list in 130ms. You can see the score deltas and a confidence break down in the JSON response.
[05:44] María: Nice. The explanation — is that deterministic? Can we get token-level highlights for why an item was boosted?
[05:50] Jin: We provide feature attributions via the "explain" flag; it adds a top-k token attention highlights, but it's slightly heavier in compute. For production we usually store rerank scores and run offline analysis.

[06:10] Aisha: On data security — we need assurance data won't be used to train models, and we need KMS integration for keys.
[06:17] Samir: Short answer: hosted API by default is customer-data-isolated and we have contractual no-training clauses in enterprise plans. We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we can offer KMS integration for certain tiers. We'll send the SOC2 and privacy addendum.

[06:40] Tom: For EU residency, can hosted be pinned to EU-only and provide audit logs?
[06:44] Samir: Yes — region pinning and audit logging are standard. If you need VPC peering or air-gapped, Private deployment is available.

[06:55] María: About SLA — latency and uptime?
[06:59] Samir: Hosted has a published SLO; Dedicated comes with contractual SLA and a latency floor guarantee. We'll share the SLA doc.

[07:10] Jin: Back to demo — I'll show how you can run a local benchmark via our CLI. (typing) The harness will call embed->retrieve->rerank and emit token / ms / cost per call. We can run this against your sample data to produce a pilot report.
[07:30] Jin: I'll trigger a small benchmark run now against 5k samples to show output. (few seconds) Results: avg end-to-end 190ms, p95 330ms, cost estimate $0.0025 per call at current config. These numbers are synthetic of course.
[07:50] María: That cost looks promising. Can we get per-route dashboards?
[07:53] Samir: Yes, Console shows per-route token breakdown and cost. You can set alerting on regressions and soft-falls where it auto-fails over to a cheaper model.

[08:10] Aisha: We use a custom embedding index built on top of FAISS and a search layer in Kubernetes. Any special adapter work?
[08:18] Jin: No heavy lift — we give you a small client lib and sample code. Integration points: batch embedding ingestion and then a standard retrieval call. For rerank we simply POST candidates. We also have examples for FAISS and Milvus.

[08:34] Tom: During the pilot, we'll need an integration path that doesn't touch PII. We'll strip user data; can you confirm any log retention?
[08:41] Samir: Hosted default retains logs 30 days, but enterprise/pilot can change retention and we can disable persistent logs if required. We'll include retention options in the SOW.

[09:00] (slightly later in the meeting, ~mid-call)
[09:05] Jin: Quick note on model variants — there are specific reranker variants that are quantization-friendly. If you accept small tradeoff in absolute MAP we can knock cost substantially by using int8 scheduling. Optimize suggests the candidate profile for your workload.
[09:22] Aisha: I'd like to see quality numbers on SKU disambiguation. We'll provide a labelled test set and you can run the eval.
[09:28] Jin: Perfect — send the labelled CSV and we'll run eval before the benchmark.

[09:40] María: Any risk around black-box scoring for compliance? We need some explainability for consumer disputes.
[09:46] Samir: We can surface attributions and historical decision logs; those are included in enterprise packages.

[10:00] Tom: Competitor question — we did a spike with Pinecone + an LLM endpoint; cost was similar but integration was more ad-hoc. How is Redwood different?
[10:10] Samir: Main difference is the unified runtime with production-grade routing, automatic batching + cache, and integrated reranker APIs. Also the Optimize tooling gives recommendations specific to your workload so you don't iterate blindly.

[10:28] (questions rapid-fire)
[10:30] María: Licensing model?
[10:32] Samir: Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved commitment, Private is license + support. We'll include numbers in the pricing doc.

[10:40] Aisha: Do you have refs doing e-commerce specifically?
[10:43] Samir: Yes — a couple of names we can share as references after NDA — I'll follow up.

[10:50] Jin: One more demo snippet — Console trace view: you can click into a specific query and see tokens, model calls, timings, and rerank scores. This helps debug when reranker changes cause surprises.
[11:05] Tom: That trace view will be helpful for us.

[11:12] (close to end)
[11:15] Samir: To recap: we'll send pilot pricing and a SOW by Thu 8/14, Jin will prepare the benchmark harness by 8/15, and Aisha will share a sanitized dataset by Wed 8/13. We'll plan the benchmark the week of 8/18.
[11:33] María: Sounds good. One ask — include EU-only hosting and a clear rollback plan if we see quality regressions.
[11:40] Samir: Absolutely, we'll call that out in SOW.

[11:45] Tom: Any blockers from our side? We'll need legal to review the SOW but otherwise should be OK.
[11:49] Samir: Great. Thank you everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

[11:55] (meeting end)
